title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study (Revision addressing topology‑cluster preregistration)
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench, a paired comparison of a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline on 1,200 intent→config episodes (preregistration rX4f7-1). Using the requested model gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator, and Mininet‑style emulation, we applied a preregistered binary episode success rule (validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback). Of 1,200 planned pairs we completed 1,199. Baseline success = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149); guarded success = 1,199/1,199 (1.0000000000). The paired‑success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025020851 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.0058381985], bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Important preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) was not executed; only the pooled paired analysis is archived. Representative artifacts show repair was invoked three times and the run used 1,203 model calls. Given the near‑ceiling baseline, the experiment was underpowered to detect very small absolute gains under the preregistered MDE (5 percentage points). We explicitly disclose the preregistration and artifact pointers for reproducibility and clarify the shared_initial_candidate design choice and its effect on repair invocation and interpretation.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent expressed in natural language into executable device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Prior system and survey literature emphasizes that operational reliability depends on the orchestration and deterministic validators that surround an LLM rather than on the base model alone. Generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) architectures are a canonical mitigation strategy: an LLM proposes candidates, a deterministic verifier checks constraints and safety, and an automated repair loop may be invoked. NetOpsTraceBench was preregistered (study_id = rX4f7-1) to provide a reproducible, workflow‑centered, paired evaluation that measures a rollback‑aware binary episode success metric comparing (A) a baseline one‑shot NL→config generation and (B) a guarded generate–validate–repair pipeline. The principal research question was: can such a paired benchmark reliably distinguish verifier‑assisted pipelines from one‑shot generation under controlled emulation? Our main contributions are (1) the preregistered paired design and full execution artifacts (rX4f7-1); (2) the pooled confirmatory analysis on 1,199 completed pairs using the requested model gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator; and (3) a transparent correction and clarification that the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory breakdown (H3) was not executed—see Methods and Disclosure for artifact locations.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers frame LLMs as components inside broader AIOps/NetOps workflows and repeatedly argue that correctness and trustworthiness are properties of the orchestration stack (model + verifier + provenance + sandboxed execution), not of the base LLM alone [http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12708/229494; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13389]. Generator+verifier loops appear in NL→formal translation and topology compilation work, and several prototype NetOps tools implement LLM proposals guarded by deterministic validators or "LLM firewalls" that enforce syntactic and semantic constraints [http://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09369; https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6947162; https://doi.org/10.3390/app16010085]. These prior results motivate workflow‑centered evaluation but also show that measured gains depend strongly on task selection, verifier strictness, and dataset construction. NetOpsTraceBench operationalizes preregistration, deterministic task generation, and emulator grounding to make such dependencies observable and reproducible.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The study preregistration (rX4f7-1, preregistration SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) froze hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion rules, seeds, stopping rules, maximum model calls (2,400), and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered confirmatory H1 required a paired test at α=0.05; the preregistered power plan targeted a minimum detectable effect (MDE) of 5 percentage points under assumed baseline ≈0.70.

Task corpus, topologies, and contamination: The benchmark scope defined 1,200 deterministically generated tasks split into two simulated topology clusters (edge=600, core=600) using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (generator_version=5.0) with frozen per‑task seeds. Each task payload included initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a declared difficulty label. The preregistration also specified contamination detection (token/subsequence overlap threshold T_contam = 0.85 and optional embedding similarity threshold 0.92) and deterministic exclusion rules; no contamination exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty).

Paired pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate design: We implemented two paired episodes per task using a shared initial candidate generation semantics: for each task a single initial LLM generation (shared_initial_candidate) was produced and then evaluated in both conditions (baseline vs guarded) to isolate the verifier/repair effect while holding generation variability constant. Rationale: the shared_initial_candidate design increases internal validity by ensuring differences arise from verifier/repair logic rather than from independent generation variability. A documented operational effect of this choice is reduced observed repair invocation (execution/execution_manifest.json shows stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 1,200 and repair = 3), because many shared initial candidates already satisfied the deterministic validator.

Pipeline implementations and deterministic validator: Adapter orchestration used hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the requested_model recorded in execution/model_configuration.json was gpt-5-mini (max_output_tokens=1500). The baseline condition takes the shared_initial_candidate and proceeds to deterministic parsing and emulator preflight checks without repair. The guarded condition runs the same shared_initial_candidate through deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version=5.0); if rejected, a single permitted repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) may be invoked per preregistration. The validator emits structured diagnostics (validation_before/validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, repair_applied boolean) that determine the binary verifier acceptance.

Binary episode success and analysis executor: The preregistered binary episode success requires (1) validation_after.valid == true, (2) emulator execution with no availability degradation above tolerance, and (3) no automatic rollback event. The archived confirmatory analysis used the analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1, computing the paired contingency table, an exact McNemar two‑sided test for paired binary outcomes, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). Note on preregistration deviation: the preregistration anticipated a nonparametric paired signed‑rank style approach; because outcomes are strictly binary the archived confirmatory test used exact McNemar—this analytic choice is documented in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/results.json.

Clarification re H3 (topology‑cluster breakdown): The preregistration included H3 (confirmatory consistency across two simulated topology clusters). The archived execution and confirmatory analysis artifacts contain only the pooled paired analysis; a preregistered per‑cluster confirmatory inference (H3) was not executed. For reproducibility and reviewer verification, the pooled analysis artifacts are archived and referenced below (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json) and the execution manifest records run accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json). Any manuscript language that previously implied a completed H3 confirmatory inference has been corrected to state explicitly that only the pooled confirmatory analysis was executed and archived.
sections.results:
Execution and pair accounting: The run completed 2,398 of 2,400 planned episodes and produced 1,199 complete paired observations (complete_pairs = 1,199; failed_episode_count = 2). Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202; repair stage calls = 3 (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Primary pooled outcomes (archived pooled analysis): The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 1,196, n10 = 3, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline_success_count = 1,196 (baseline_success_rate = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076). Guarded_success_count = 1,199 (guarded_success_rate = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0). Observed paired‑success‑rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25 (analysis/results.json). Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957] computed with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Missingness and exclusions: The preregistered deterministic exclusion rules produced no contamination exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty). Missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv): complete_pairs = 1,199; both_missing_pairs = 1; failed_baseline_episodes = 1; failed_guarded_episodes = 1.

Repair and difficulty diagnostics: Stage_counts indicate repair = 3 while shared_initial_generation = 1,200, matching repair_provider traces for three episodes. Representative per‑episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) show validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false for the large majority of episodes, and task_manifest entries indicate heterogeneous declared difficulty across the corpus (examples labeled "medium", "hard", "very_hard"). These artifacts demonstrate that under the deterministic task generator and validator settings many initial candidates satisfied intent constraints, explaining low repair invocation.

Topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis H3: As stated in Methods, the preregistered per‑cluster confirmatory test H3 was not executed; only the pooled analysis above is archived. The pooled artifacts named above are the basis for the confirmatory inference reported here.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation: The pooled confirmatory analysis yields no statistically significant advantage for the guarded pipeline (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% CI includes zero). Two artifact‑grounded explanations are supported. First, near‑ceiling baseline performance (≈99.75%) greatly reduced headroom for absolute improvement versus the preregistered MDE (5 percentage points). The small number of discordant pairs (n10 = 3, n01 = 0) produces low statistical resolution for detecting tiny absolute gains, which is reflected in the archived bootstrap CI and exact test. Second, the shared_initial_candidate design and the chosen deterministic task generator/validator configuration reduced repair invocation: the run invoked repair only three times (execution/execution_manifest.json), indicating that many initial candidates already satisfied validator checks. These two factors—high baseline and design choices intended to isolate verifier effects—explain the observed null result in the pooled analysis without implying verifiers are universally unhelpful.

Implications for benchmarking and future work: To reveal verifier benefits a benchmark should increase task ambiguity/adversariality, vary verifier strictness, or test multiple model families and independent generation semantics (i.e., not sharing the same initial candidate between conditions). The archived artifacts here (task manifests, validator traces, provider audits, and analysis code) provide a reproducible baseline from which targeted sensitivity experiments (varying difficulty, verifier thresholds, or independent generation) can be launched.

Threats to validity and externality: Internal validity is strong due to frozen seeds and deterministic generators/validators; construct validity depends on whether the preregistered binary episode success maps to operationally meaningful correctness across production environments; emulator fidelity is limited compared to diverse vendor production idiosyncrasies; and external validity is constrained by testing a single requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a primarily synthetic/consented task corpus. The preregistered per‑cluster confirmatory H3 was not executed, which further limits claims about topology‑cluster consistency (see Methods and archived artifacts).
sections.conclusion: NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1) produced an artifact‑rich, preregistered pooled paired analysis comparing one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→config pipelines on 1,199 completed pairs. Under the chosen deterministic task generator, validator configuration, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and requested model (gpt-5-mini), baseline one‑shot performance was near ceiling and the guarded pipeline produced a small absolute gain (≈0.25 percentage points) that was not statistically significant under the preregistered inferential framework (exact McNemar p = 0.25; 95% bootstrap CI includes zero). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) was not executed and that only the pooled confirmatory analysis is archived; pooled analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json) and execution accounting (execution/execution_manifest.json) are provided to support reproducible interpretation. The run artifacts support follow‑up sensitivity studies that intentionally vary corpus difficulty, verifier strictness, and generation semantics to identify conditions under which verifier scaffolding yields operationally meaningful improvements. All archived artifacts, seeds, provider traces, and analysis code are referenced in the Disclosure Statement for exact reproduction and follow‑up work.

limitations: Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture all deployment failure modes (routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, transient telemetry).

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary. This deviation is recorded in analysis artifacts.
Topology‑cluster confirmatory hypothesis (H3) preregistered but not executed; only pooled confirmatory analysis is archived, which limits claims about per‑cluster consistency.
